spec_match.rationale: Uses the real product pattern the spec names for these setters — declaring capture state alongside togglemicrophone/togglecamera action handlers — and surfaces each call's actual settled result, which is the 158 change.

interactive.rationale: Two aria-pressed toggles drive live setter calls, a declared-state readout, and a settled-result log; real setActionHandler registrations let browser/OS UI drive the same paths.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index promises a control bar wiring action handlers to the setters with a settled-result log; delivered, including the acknowledgement framing.

edge_cases.rationale: Handles unsupported browsers, setActionHandler rejection, and setter failure (state does not flip on failure), but the NotAllowedError pause-policy branch is only explained, not exercisable — no deterministic way to trigger it from a page.

references.rationale: Links chromestatus.com/feature/5188639100370944 and the setCameraActive spec anchor.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite covers the setter surface and the 158 promise contract this page's log reports; the page adds the product context on top.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 153 CDP driver: mic toggled true→false→true by click and again by Enter key, camera toggled, declared-state lines and log updated with the real pre-158 'returned undefined' outcomes, both handlers registered, zero console/page errors, zero failed requests, 0px overflow both classes.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts per-toggle success, handler registration count, and the unsupported fallback branch separately.

design_system.rationale: Toggle buttons invert both background and color in the pressed state (the button bg+color rule), all colours are tokens, log entries are charcoal on stone.

accessibility.rationale: Toggles are native buttons with aria-pressed and visible text state, the bar is a labelled group, the log is a polite live region, keyboard activation verified with Enter.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: The call bar wraps on narrow viewports; 0px overflow at 360×740 DPR3 and 1280×800; toggles are 44px-min targets.

openQuestions.title: Exercise the toggles during real capture on a 158+ build
openQuestions.detail: With a granted getUserMedia stream on Chrome 158+, the same toggles should resolve their promises while the tab's capture indicator and OS media hub reflect the declared state. That end-to-end acknowledgement (and any NotAllowedError under a UA pause policy) needs a real permissioned session to observe; this page deliberately stays permission-free since the changed surface is the return value.

guidanceConsulted.query: toggle buttons aria-pressed state and keyboard activation
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use native buttons with aria-pressed for binary toggles, keep the visible label in sync with the state, and never rely on colour alone.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Mic/camera are native buttons with aria-pressed plus text labels (Mic: on / Mic: muted); pressed state also inverts bg/colour; Enter-key activation verified in the driver.

guidanceConsulted.query: disabled state during in-flight async action
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Disable the triggering control while its async action is pending and re-enable on settlement so repeated activation cannot interleave.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Each toggle disables itself during the declare() await and re-enables after; repeated clicking in the driver produced strictly ordered log entries.

summary: A permission-free in-call control bar: aria-pressed toggles declare capture state through the real setters, togglemicrophone/togglecamera handlers are genuinely registered, and the settled-result log shows exactly what this build returned (undefined on 153, the acknowledgement promise on 158+). Verified with the headless Chromium 153 CDP driver: click and keyboard toggles, state lines, handler registration, clean console/network, ok/ok responsive matrix.
